title: The Operational Facilitator's alignment finding is a hard gate that stops a proposal before token holders ever vote
content:
A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.3 requires the Operational Facilitator to review each Root Edit Proposal for alignment within seven days, announcing either an aligned finding or a misaligned one "and provide the reasoning for it." A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4 then makes the vote conditional: the poll is triggered "where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Osero Artifact."

The implication is that a misalignment finding terminates the proposal. The Routine Protocol specifies no appeal, no supermajority override, and no route by which OSERO holders can put a rejected proposal to a vote anyway.

This is a deliberate constraint on token-holder sovereignty, and it is the same design logic as Alignment Conservers elsewhere in the Atlas: rather than trusting an electorate to reject misaligned proposals, the system prevents misaligned proposals from reaching the electorate. It raises the alignment floor without requiring holders to be aligned.

The cost is a single point of governance failure. Everything depends on the Facilitator's independence and competence, since a captured or mistaken Facilitator can silently narrow the option set holders ever see. Only the requirement to publish reasoning on the Forum constrains that power — reputational pressure rather than procedural recourse.

The tension sharpens when read with A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.2, which defers guidelines for expert review of technically complex proposals to a future iteration: the sole gatekeeper currently has no defined access to specialist analysis.
description: A misalignment finding ends the process at the review stage — the Artifact defines no appeal, override, or holder path to force a poll against the Facilitator's judgment.
